resources.string:
Lingua Link Ledger (PET) records seed-batch evidence on this phone. This test version, App v1, sends nothing to any server or gateway: every record stays on the phone.

Record a stage
Each stage is recorded by photographing the batch's label with the phone's camera. The app reads the batch ID from the label's QR code; if it cannot, take the photo again, or type the ID printed on the label. Every record needs the phone's position: a GPS fix, or a location set by hand in ATAK, shown as "Manual location - not GPS". Nothing is saved until you tap Save. Each record is saved on this phone as a package of its photos and their details, with the package's SHA-256.
• Collecting: a new collection batch, under a label not recorded before.
• Cleaning: combines one or more collection batches into a new batch with a new label. Photograph each batch being cleaned, then the new label. The batches combined are closed, and cannot be combined again.
• Stored: record one batch in storage (a batch at Cleaning, or stored before), or tap Combine batches to combine batches at Cleaning or Stored into a new batch with a new label, as at Cleaning. A batch cannot be stored before it is cleaned.
• Planting: a batch in storage is sown. The batch then closes and takes no more events.

Status
Shows that no gateway is set up yet, how many records are saved on this phone (and how many from the tools), and the app version.

Look up batch
Photograph one batch label with the phone's camera. The app reads the batch ID from the label's QR code and shows it, with TEST LABEL for a simulated label, the species as printed on the label (not checked), and where the phone is. It also shows what this phone has recorded for that batch (its stage, whether it is closed and why, what it was combined from, and its events) and which stage to record next; or, for a batch not recorded yet, that it starts at Collecting. It records nothing, and the photo is deleted once it has been read. Hold the phone so the label fills much of the photo, and photograph one label at a time: a photo with two codes is refused.

Saved batches
Every batch this phone has recorded, with its stage, open or closed. Tap one to see what it was combined from and its events: the stage, the time (UTC), the position with its source and accuracy, and the package with its full SHA-256. Records from the tools are listed after the batches. Nothing is recorded from this list.

Tools
• Create/Edit Data Package: write a metadata file (the package name, description and author, typed and not checked; a stage; and the phone's position, by the same rules as above). The plugin then builds an ATAK data package named from the Package Name, holding that file, and adds it to ATAK's Data Packages list; it says what it built. The plugin keeps the metadata file's SHA-256, so it can tell the packages it built from any other .zip.
• Create Evidence Trace: choose one of the data packages built with Create/Edit Data Package (no other file is offered). Its SHA-256 is calculated and saved on this phone, with the stage and position from its metadata. A package is traced once.
• Add Stage Event: choose one of the evidence traces saved on this phone, pick a stage, and save it with the phone's position and optional remarks (typed, not checked).
• Send Data Package: choose a data package and send it with ATAK's own Send dialog, to contacts or to a TAK Server this phone is set up for. That is ATAK sending, not the PET gateway. The package's SHA-256 is shown before ATAK's dialog opens.

Where the records are
Every record stays on this phone, in atak/tools/lingualinkledger in its storage: ledger.json, the packages folder and the tool_records folder. They are plain files, and each holds the phone's real position. The app cannot delete them; the install guide says how to clear test records.

A note on words: in ATAK, a "data package" is a .zip of files to share with other TAK users. PET's evidence records are built from such packages, and each record keeps its package's SHA-256.
